story.title: Catastrophic Floods in Nepal and Tibet Leave Hundreds Dead and Missing
story.summary: Catastrophic floods triggered by a glacial collapse near the Nepal-China border have resulted in at least 160 confirmed deaths, with over 1,300 people reported missing. Rescue teams are actively searching for the missing individuals, including a significant number of foreigners. The floods, which swept through communities, were exacerbated by ongoing monsoon rains in the region.
sources: AP - Top News via Google News

event_overview.title: About Natural Disasters
event_overview.subject: Natural Disasters
event_overview.summary: Natural disasters are serious disruptions to communities or societies caused when hazardous events interact with exposure, vulnerability and limited capacity to cope. This timeline concerns sudden-onset hydro-meteorological disasters in Asia, including tropical-cyclone impacts and flooding, rather than treating the hazards alone as disasters.

facts.label: Definition
facts.value: UNDRR defines a disaster as a serious disruption of a community or society caused by hazardous events interacting with exposure, vulnerability and capacity, producing human, material, economic or environmental losses.

facts.label: Hazard types
facts.value: The events in this timeline fall primarily within hydro-meteorological hazards: tropical cyclones are large, non-frontal storms that originate over tropical oceans, while flooding is a hydrological hazard.

facts.label: Tropical-storm classification
facts.value: Under WMO classification, a tropical storm has maximum sustained winds above 63 km/h (34 knots) and below tropical-cyclone/typhoon strength; storms in the western North Pacific and South China Sea are named by RSMC Tokyo–Typhoon Centre using the ESCAP/WMO Typhoon Committee list.

facts.label: Disaster-risk framework
facts.value: The Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction covers 2015–2030. Adopted on March 18, 2015, it sets seven global targets and four priorities: understanding risk, strengthening risk governance, investing in resilience, and preparedness and recovery.

facts.label: Response and health
facts.value: Disaster risk management spans prevention and mitigation, preparedness, response and recovery; health risks can arise when disasters damage shelter, water, sanitation, waste-management systems and other infrastructure.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline highlights the specified 2026 flooding and tropical-storm developments in eastern China, Nepal and Tibet; it does not attempt to catalog all natural hazards, disaster losses, emergency responses or weather events worldwide.

explore_lenses.label: Why does this disaster matter beyond Rasuwa?
explore_lenses.title: A fast-moving cross-border river crisis
explore_lenses.summary: The flood affected a river corridor linking Nepal and Tibet, damaging essential infrastructure and involving visitors from dozens of countries. Its downstream reach turned a high-mountain collapse into a wider public-safety and humanitarian response.

claims.text: Nepal's government said the August 26 flood damaged homes, schools, hospitals, roads, bridges and hydropower facilities, alongside causing displacement and loss of life.

An initial technical assessment reported that the surge moved through the Bhotekoshi, Trishuli and Narayani river systems over roughly 10 hours, creating risk well beyond the initial border-area impact zone.

The scale of foreign-national involvement has made consular coordination a major part of the response: Nepal's Foreign Ministry created an emergency control room for search, verification and assistance involving affected foreigners.

explore_lenses.label: How did a glacier collapse cause such flooding?
explore_lenses.title: A cascading ice, rock and debris event
explore_lenses.summary: The leading explanation is that a high-altitude ice-and-rock collapse sent debris into the Lhende Khola, producing an exceptionally rapid, sediment-heavy flood wave. Scientists are still determining the precise sequence and whether temporary river damming worsened the surge.

claims.text: ICIMOD's preliminary assessment said ice and rock debris likely entered the Lende Khola, a Bhote Koshi tributary, generating a sudden downstream surge carrying water, sediment and boulders.

Satellite-image analysis reviewed by geomorphologists indicated that bedrock beneath part of the Langtang Lirung glacier collapsed as well, bringing a large mass of ice, rock and boulders into the valley.

ICIMOD reported water-level rises of as much as nine metres at Galchchi within 30 minutes and seven metres at Malekhu over a similar period, illustrating why downstream warning and evacuation time was limited.
ICIMOD says the ice-avalanche trigger, any debris dam and its stability, and the role of climate change in this individual event remain unconfirmed or too early to determine.

explore_lenses.label: What happens next for survivors and missing people?
explore_lenses.title: Searches, verification and renewed flood monitoring
explore_lenses.summary: Nepal's immediate priorities are rescue, evacuation, medical care and relief, while authorities verify identities and missing-person reports. Monitoring remains important because the original event damaged some gauging stations and experts warned of possible continuing upstream hazards.

claims.text: The Government of Nepal said it had mobilized search and rescue, evacuation, emergency medical assistance and relief operations, while continuing to assess needs and flood risks.

Nepal's Foreign Ministry asked diplomatic missions, international organizations and families to use its emergency control room to provide information on affected foreign nationals and urged reliance on official updates rather than unverified reports.

Forecast: ICIMOD said that a possible upstream blockage could create a secondary flood hazard if impounded water is released suddenly; it reported that authorities had issued evacuation orders for Jilong port while the blockage was assessed.
Several river-monitoring stations stopped transmitting or were reportedly washed away during the event, although warnings were still issued using available data and incoming reports.

story_report.summary: Flooding triggered by a glacial collapse near the Nepal-China border has killed at least 160 people and left more than 1,300 others reported missing in Nepal and Tibet. Rescue operations are continuing in the border region as authorities work to locate those unaccounted for. The disaster has also damaged essential infrastructure and displaced residents, while the fast-moving surge spread through multiple river systems, extending the danger beyond the initial impact area.

sections.heading: Surge Moved Through River Systems
sections.body: A preliminary technical assessment said the flood travelled through the Bhotekoshi, Trishuli and Narayani river systems over roughly 10 hours. ICIMOD said ice and rock debris likely entered the Lende Khola, a Bhote Koshi tributary, producing a sudden downstream surge carrying water, sediment and boulders. At Galchchi, water levels rose by as much as nine metres within 30 minutes; Malekhu recorded a seven-metre rise over a similar period.

sections.heading: Infrastructure Damage and Foreign-National Response
sections.body: Nepal’s government said the August 26 flood damaged homes, schools, hospitals, roads, bridges and hydropower facilities, in addition to causing deaths and displacement. Search and rescue teams, evacuation operations, emergency medical assistance and relief efforts have been mobilized while needs and flood risks are assessed. Nepal’s Foreign Ministry has opened an emergency control room for information, verification and assistance involving affected foreign nationals, asking diplomatic missions, organizations and families to use official channels.

sections.heading: Monitoring Gaps and Secondary Flood Risk
sections.body: Several river-monitoring stations stopped transmitting or were reportedly swept away during the flooding, though authorities continued issuing warnings using available data and incoming reports. ICIMOD said a possible upstream blockage could pose a secondary flood risk if impounded water is released suddenly. Authorities issued evacuation orders for Jilong port while assessing the blockage, according to ICIMOD.

unresolved.text: Death and missing-person counts remain subject to verification. It is not yet clear how many people listed as missing are stranded, injured, dead, duplicated across records or safely out of contact.

Scientists are still investigating the physical trigger of the flood. ICIMOD said the ice-avalanche trigger, the existence and stability of any debris dam, and climate change’s role in this individual event have not been confirmed or are too early to determine.

The attacks have ignited fires across these areas, marking a significant escalation in hostilities.

related_stories.title: Jury Begins Deliberations in Lindsay Clancy Murder Trial
related_stories.summary: The jury is currently deliberating in the trial of Lindsay Clancy, who is accused of killing her three children. During closing arguments, the defense argued that Clancy was suffering from postpartum psychosis, while prosecutors claimed she intentionally planned the murders. The outcome now rests with the jury.
